objective: Prove that the sphere's count needs polynomial-calculus degree at least c n^{1/4}/log n over every field, F2 included: the functional pigeonhole principle on a bounded-degree boundary expander (Miksa and Nordstrom: degree linear in the holes over every field) reduces by shallow decision trees to LeftPigeon and, through COUNT-SYSTEMS-20261110-001A's chain, to the count, and polynomial-calculus degree transfers through such reductions. With TREE-XOR-20261110-001B this gives tree-like Res(xor) size 2^{Omega(n^{1/4}/log n)} and improves TREE-XOR-20261110-001A's depth bound to the same order.
status: Proved 2026-11-10 (from Miksa and Nordstrom's degree bound and the program's reductions): over every field the count needs polynomial-calculus degree at least c n^{1/4}/log n; over F2, tree-like Res(xor) size 2^{Omega(n^{1/4}/log n)} and parity-tree depth Omega(n^{1/4}/log n). Known-with-delta, folklore risk high.
title: The count needs F2 polynomial-calculus degree n^{Omega(1)}
